guards.note: Every seed ran both arms to the end of the window.
In every seed, control and treatment were in identical states until the intervention.

success.note: Mean treatment − control difference is at least 0.01 count in the expected direction.
Every seed moved in the expected direction.

failure.note: No mean difference, or one in the opposite direction.

limitations: Simulated: this describes the Bethesda simulator (bethesda-city/4), not Bethesda. Agents follow illustrative rules that respond to the event's declared effects; no crowd, fire, weather or transit physics is modelled.
Population is the pre-registered experiment profile (40 pedestrians, 8 cars, 2 buses), not measured demand; routines and schedules are illustrative.
3 seeds: a small sample. The result is descriptive and no significance test is computed.
World observations are sampled every 100 ticks (10 simulated seconds); behaviour between samples is not measured.

charter.covers: Native Bethesda experiments plus a research program using the pinned corpus, mathematical index, four local-model perspectives and draft manuscript artifacts. Public Crossref query text is permitted only when explicitly enabled in the research scope. No arbitrary code execution or external-world interventions.

research.goal: How do different simulated urban disruptions alter collective movement patterns, and under which conditions does the same intervention produce different behavioral outcomes?
